Buenaventura Durruti.fact: At 06:00, on 19 November, Durruti met Mera at the Directorate-General and together they went up the building's tower to observe the offensive.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: By 07:00, they had seen their forces had taken some of the floors in the _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Mera and Durruti then agreed to meet the following morning, at the Directorate-General of the Civil Guard, from which Durruti would lead an offensive to capture the Hospital Clinic. By 07:00, they had seen their forces had taken some of the floors in the Hospital Clinic.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: To free the trapped militiamen, he ordered two companies from a reserve battalion to attack the _____'s ground floor
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: By 07:00, they had seen their forces had taken some of the floors in the Hospital Clinic. To free the trapped militiamen, he ordered two companies from a reserve battalion to attack the Clinic's ground floor.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: After a bullet almost hit Durruti, he and _____ decided to leave the tower and go back down to the street
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: After a bullet almost hit Durruti, he and Mera decided to leave the tower and go back down to the street. There he agreed to Mera's proposal that they join their forces under his command and enforce strict discipline, but he remained immediately preoccupied with relieving his men as soon as possible, and told Mera they would revisit the issue in their meeting with Val later that day.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: At 12:30, Durruti returned to his headquarters to hear an update from _____, who passed on a message from Mira begging for relief
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: At 12:30, Durruti returned to his headquarters to hear an update from Mora, who passed on a message from Mira begging for relief.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: He responded to _____ that he had to stay in his post until their men were replaced later that day, and prepared a relief order to be approved by Miaja
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: At 12:30, Durruti returned to his headquarters to hear an update from Mora, who passed on a message from Mira begging for relief. He responded to Mira that he had to stay in his post until their men were replaced later that day, and prepared a relief order to be approved by Miaja.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti decided to see the situation in person and headed for the front in his _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti decided to see the situation in person and headed for the front in his Packard.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: It is unclear who was responsible, with various hypotheses blaming either the _____, Stalinists or Durruti's own militiamen for the shooting
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: It is unclear who was responsible, with various hypotheses blaming either the Nationalists, Stalinists or Durruti's own militiamen for the shooting.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: His driver rushed to get him back in the car and take him to the column's military hospital at the _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: His driver rushed to get him back in the car and take him to the column's military hospital at the Ritz Hotel.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti died in his hospital bed at 04:00 on 20 November _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti died in his hospital bed at 04:00 on 20 November 1936.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: His body was taken to _____ the following day, and his funeral was held on 23 November
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: His body was taken to Barcelona the following day, and his funeral was held on 23 November.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: His funeral was attended by an estimated 500,000 people, and the procession was headed by Lluís Companys, _____ and the consuls from Mexico and the Soviet Union
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: His funeral was attended by an estimated 500,000 people, and the procession was headed by Lluís Companys, Joan Garcia Oliver and the consuls from Mexico and the Soviet Union.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti was remembered as a criminal by the _____ upper classes and right-wing, and as a martyr by his fellow revolutionaries
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti was remembered as a criminal by the Spanish upper classes and right-wing, and as a martyr by his fellow revolutionaries. He became a central figure in the history of early 20th century Spain, and in histories of the Spanish anarchist movement in particular, as his life was considered to be representative of many other Spanish anarchists.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: The poet León _____ declared that Durruti's life would inspire a "legion of Durrutis" to follow in his footsteps, although historian Hugh Thomas said that Felipe was wrong to believe this
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The poet León Felipe declared that Durruti's life would inspire a "legion of Durrutis" to follow in his footsteps, although historian Hugh Thomas said that Felipe was wrong to believe this.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: She described him as the "very soul of the _____ revolution" and depicted him as a personification of Spain itself
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: She described him as the "very soul of the Spanish revolution" and depicted him as a personification of Spain itself. On the other hand, Federica Montseny insisted that Spanish anarchists "did not see him as a hero [or] a messiah", as they rejected leader cults.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: On the other hand, _____ insisted that Spanish anarchists "did not see him as a hero [or] a messiah", as they rejected leader cults
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: On the other hand, Federica Montseny insisted that Spanish anarchists "did not see him as a hero [or] a messiah", as they rejected leader cults.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In contrast, Nazi propagandist Karl-Georg von _____ denounced Durruti as "subhuman"
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In contrast, Nazi propagandist Karl-Georg von Stackelberg denounced Durruti as "subhuman".

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Historian Antony Beevor compared him to a "revolutionary _____", Eric Hobsbawm called him a "noble gunman", and Burnett Bolloten described him as a "legendary hero" of the Spanish anarchist movement
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Historian Antony Beevor compared him to a "revolutionary Robin Hood", Eric Hobsbawm called him a "noble gunman", and Burnett Bolloten described him as a "legendary hero" of the Spanish anarchist movement.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: According to historian _____, Durruti has been most remembered for "his role as the most proletarian European revolutionary leader"
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: According to historian Robert Kern, Durruti has been most remembered for "his role as the most proletarian European revolutionary leader".

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Historian Hugh Thomas described Durruti as having had "dreams of grandeur", but _____, who had met Durruti before his death, disputed this characterisation
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Historian Antony Beevor compared him to a "revolutionary Robin Hood", Eric Hobsbawm called him a "noble gunman", and Burnett Bolloten described him as a "legendary hero" of the Spanish anarchist movement. Historian Hugh Thomas described Durruti as having had "dreams of grandeur", but Bolloten, who had met Durruti before his death, disputed this characterisation.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: On this, Kern also compared Durruti with the Argentine revolutionary _____, due to their shared populist ideology and revolutionary leadership qualities
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: On this, Kern also compared Durruti with the Argentine revolutionary Che Guevara, due to their shared populist ideology and revolutionary leadership qualities.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Anarchist historians such as _____ would present Durruti as an "intransigent opponent of militarisation", but this characterisation is likewise disputed by other historians, including Julián Casanova
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Anarchist historians such as Abel Paz would present Durruti as an "intransigent opponent of militarisation", but this characterisation is likewise disputed by other historians, including Julián Casanova.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: English communist _____ described Durruti as "an anarchist who fell as a disciplined member of the Spanish people's army" and believed his death was a loss to all Spanish republicans
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: English communist Humphrey Slater described Durruti as "an anarchist who fell as a disciplined member of the Spanish people's army" and believed his death was a loss to all Spanish republicans.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti's life and deeds were also celebrated by both civilians and state officials in the _____, where he was the only anarchist to receive coverage in the Stalinist press
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti's life and deeds were also celebrated by both civilians and state officials in the Soviet Union, where he was the only anarchist to receive coverage in the Stalinist press.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: The slogan was later used as justification by the _____ of Spain (PCE) for the repression of anarchists and Trotskyists in the Red Terror
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The slogan was later used as justification by the Communist Party of Spain (PCE) for the repression of anarchists and Trotskyists in the Red Terror.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Émilienne Morin also reported that the Catholic Church, which had previously denounced Durruti for his anti-clericalism, later sought to canonise him as a "red Jesus".

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: His daughter _____ likewise reported that "now he’s dead, they all want to claim him for their own [...] a dead revolutionary is always a good revolutionary"
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: His daughter Colette likewise reported that "now he’s dead, they all want to claim him for their own [...] a dead revolutionary is always a good revolutionary".

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: After his death, Barcelona's Via Laietana was renamed to Via Durruti.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In 1937, a newly set up hospital in Binéfar was named after Durruti. In March 1937, the Catalan anarchist journalist Jaume Balius set up the Friends of Durruti Group, named after Durruti.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In March _____, the Catalan anarchist journalist Jaume Balius established the Friends of Durruti Group, named after Durruti
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In 1937, a newly set up hospital in Binéfar was named after Durruti. In March 1937, the Catalan anarchist journalist Jaume Balius set up the Friends of Durruti Group, named after Durruti.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: An orphanage named after Durruti and Ascaso was established in _____, where it housed 200 refugee children from Madrid
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: An orphanage named after Durruti and Ascaso was set up in Figueres, where it housed 200 refugee children from Madrid.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: This group sought to oppose the policies of the CNT-FAI leadership, which it considered "counterrevolutionary", and aligned itself with _____ organisations
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: This group sought to oppose the policies of the CNT-FAI leadership, which it considered "counterrevolutionary", and aligned itself with Trotskyist organisations.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti's death resulted in a loss of morale and enthusiasm among many Spanish revolutionaries. Buenaventura Durruti.question: In the months after his death, the anarchist movement became increasingly disorientated and divided, and lost much of its influence in the _____ to the communists
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In the months after his death, the anarchist movement became increasingly disorientated and divided, and lost much of its influence in the Republic to the communists.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The Nationalists ultimately won the civil war on 1 April 1939.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: After the _____ transition to democracy in the late 1970s, a square in Barcelona was renamed after Durruti
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: According to the anarchist historian José Luis Gutiérrez Molina, Durruti's death marked the effective end of the Spanish Revolution of 1936, which soon gave way to the dismantling of revolutionary institutions and their integration into state structures. After the Spanish transition to democracy in the late 1970s, a square in Barcelona was renamed after Durruti.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Biographies about Durruti have been written by _____, Raimundo Ferrer, Joan Llarch and Abel Paz
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Biographies about Durruti have been written by Hans Magnus Enzensberger, Raimundo Ferrer, Joan Llarch and Abel Paz.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The latter's biography on Durruti's life was originally published as Durruti: Le Peuple en Armes, in Paris in 1972.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: The book was translated from French by Nancy MacDonald, whose English language edition was published in Montreal in _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The book was translated from French by Nancy MacDonald, whose English language edition was published in Montreal in 1977.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: It also received translations into German, _____, Japanese, Portuguese and Spanish
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: It also received translations into German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Spanish.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Paz published a second, expanded edition in the Spanish language in _____, titling it Durruti en la Revolución española, and an English translation by Chuck Morse was published in 2006
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Paz published a second, expanded edition in the Spanish language in 1996, titling it Durruti en la Revolución española, and an English translation by Chuck Morse was published in 2006.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: They made their way to _____, where they were hosted by the General Confederation of Workers (CGT) until reuniting with Alejandro Ascaso and Gregorio Jover in March 1925
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: They made their way to Mexico City, where they were hosted by the General Confederation of Workers (CGT) until reuniting with Alejandro Ascaso and Gregorio Jover in March 1925.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: By November 1926, as campaigns against their extradition began to gain wider public support, _____, Durruti and Jover were notified that they were to be handed over to the Argentine police
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: By November 1926, as campaigns against their extradition began to gain wider public support, Ascaso, Durruti and Jover were notified that they were to be handed over to the Argentine police. Durruti and Ascaso accepted their own extradition, but appealed for the French government to grant clemency for Jover, who had two young children.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In January 1928, Durruti and _____ went to Paris, where they heard news from Ricardo Sanz and Joaquín Cortés about the Spanish and Argentine anarchist movements
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti and Ascaso upheld the revolutionary potential of both the proletariat and the peasantry in Spain, and believed that anarchists ought to accelerate the revolutionary process by encouraging revolutionary initiatives and staying focused on long-term goals over short-term material improvements. Durruti and Ascaso also aligned themselves against proposals to establish sections of the CNT in France, as they believed it would divert attention away from revolutionary initiatives in Spain.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: However, when Durruti and _____ arrived in Belgium in early 1929, they discovered the country had relaxed its immigration laws and become a safe haven for Spanish exiles
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti and Ascaso subsequently decided to return to Mexico. However, when Durruti and Ascaso arrived in Belgium in early 1929, they discovered the country had relaxed its immigration laws and become a safe haven for Spanish exiles.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: The Spanish press branded Durruti, Ascaso and _____ as "public enemies", culminating with Ascaso's arrest in October 1931
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The Spanish press branded Durruti, Ascaso and Joan Garcia Oliver as "public enemies", culminating with Ascaso's arrest in October 1931.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Less than a week after he sent this letter, on 4 December 1931, Emilienne Morin gave birth to their daughter _____
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Less than a week after he sent this letter, on 4 December 1931, Emilienne Morin gave birth to their daughter Colette Durruti.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: To prevent this, the Civil Guard arrested Durruti under investigation for the 1923 Gijón robbery.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: On 18 _____ 1932, insurrection broke out in the region, as workers armed themselves and proclaimed libertarian communism
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: On 18 January 1932, insurrection broke out in the region, as workers armed themselves and proclaimed libertarian communism. Durruti was arrested for his part in the insurrection, on 21 January.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: When the insurrection broke out on the evening of 8 _____ 1933, Durruti led the assault against the Travessera de Gràcia barracks, where he found that the police had already mobilised
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: When the insurrection broke out on the evening of 8 January 1933, Durruti led the assault against the Travessera de Gràcia barracks, where he found that the police had already mobilised. By the early hours of 9 January, the insurrection had failed.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: By the time of the 4th _____ of the CNT, held in Zaragoza on 1 May 1936, Durruti was looked up to as an informal leader within the organisation
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: By the time of the 4th National Congress of the CNT, held in Zaragoza on 1 May 1936, Durruti was looked up to as an informal leader within the organisation.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: He wanted to know what the anarchists were planning and admitted that the _____ government would collapse, as it did in October 1934, without their help
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: He wanted to know what the anarchists were planning and admitted that the Catalan government would collapse, as it did in October 1934, without their help. When the police chief refused to give the anarchists weapons, Durruti concluded that the Catalan government was planning to use them as "cannon fodder".

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The latter's biography on Durruti's life was originally published as Durruti: Le Peuple en Armes, in Paris in 1972.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In April 1923, Durruti travelled to Madrid, where he gave stolen money to the defense fund of Pere Mateu and Lluís Nicolau, who had been charged with murdering Eduardo Dato.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In mid-1924, _____ arrived in Paris and informed Durruti and Francisco of his plan to ignite an insurrection in Catalonia
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In mid-1924, Domingo Ascaso arrived in Paris and informed Durruti and Francisco of his plan to ignite an insurrection in Catalonia.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: By September 1924, plans for the operation were well underway, but difficulties acquiring weapons and supporters in _____ made many of the insurgents sceptical about their chances
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: By September 1924, plans for the operation were well underway, but difficulties acquiring weapons and supporters in Barcelona made many of the insurgents sceptical about their chances. Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In December 1924, Durruti and _____ set off with false passports and embarked for Cuba

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: In February 1926, _____ left South America and returned to France

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: By June 1926, Durruti, Ascaso and Jover were plotting to attack Alfonso XIII, on the occasion of the king's visit to Paris.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: The meeting ultimately resolved to schedule a national conference to make a binding decision on the proposed alliance, but before it could be held, the _____ of 1934 broke out

Cao Hong.question: After that, Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at _____ (濮陽縣; west of present-day Puyang County, Henan) and defeated him
Cao Hong.fact: After that, Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at Puyang County (濮陽縣; west of present-day Puyang County, Henan) and defeated him.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Cao subsequently attacked and retook Dong'e (東阿), Jiyin (濟陰), _____ (山陽), Zhongmu (中牟), Yangwu (陽武), Jing (京), Mi (密) and other counties from Lü Bu
Cao Hong.fact: Cao Cao subsequently attacked and retook Dong'e (東阿), Jiyin (濟陰), Shanyang (山陽), Zhongmu (中牟), Yangwu (陽武), Jing (京), Mi (密) and other counties from Lü Bu.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: In August 196, Cao Cao led his forces into Luoyang and received _____
Cao Hong.fact: In August 196, Cao Cao led his forces into Luoyang and received Emperor Xian.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages

Cao Hong.fact: Two months later, he relocated the emperor to his own base in Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), where the new imperial capital was set up. After Cao Cao left Wuyin County and returned to Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), the officials in Nanyang (南陽), Zhangling (章陵) and other counties who had surrendered to him earlier rebelled and defected to Zhang Xiu's side.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: The garrison came under multiple attacks by _____ and his ally Liu Biao
Cao Hong.fact: After Cao Cao left Wuyin County and returned to Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan), the officials in Nanyang (南陽), Zhangling (章陵) and other counties who had surrendered to him earlier rebelled and defected to Zhang Xiu's side. The garrison came under multiple attacks by Zhang Xiu and his ally Liu Biao.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Cao Cao succeeded in destroying _____'s supplies in the raid and killed Chunyu Qiong in battle
Cao Hong.fact: When both sides were locked in a stalemate around winter, Cao Cao heeded the advice of Xu You, a defector from Yuan Shao's side, and personally led 5,000 riders to raid Yuan's supply depot at Wuchao (烏巢; southeast of present-day Yanjin County, Henan), which was guarded by Chunyu Qiong. Cao Cao succeeded in destroying Yuan Shao's supplies in the raid and killed Chunyu Qiong in battle.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: When Yuan Shao heard that _____ was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao
Cao Hong.fact: When both sides were locked in a stalemate around winter, Cao Cao heeded the advice of Xu You, a defector from Yuan Shao's side, and personally led 5,000 riders to raid Yuan's supply depot at Wuchao (烏巢; southeast of present-day Yanjin County, Henan), which was guarded by Chunyu Qiong. When Yuan Shao heard that Wuchao was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: However, _____ and Gao Lan, already frustrated with Yuan Shao, ended up defecting to Cao Cao's side instead
Cao Hong.fact: When Yuan Shao heard that Wuchao was under attack, he sent his generals Zhang He and Gao Lan (高覽) to attack Cao Cao's main camp in the hope of diverting Cao's attention away from Wuchao. However, Zhang He and Gao Lan, already frustrated with Yuan Shao, ended up defecting to Cao Cao's side instead.

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: For his achievements, he was promoted to General of _____ (厲鋒將軍) and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Guoming Village (國明亭侯)
Cao Hong.fact: For his achievements, he was promoted to General of Sharp Edge (厲鋒將軍) and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Guoming Village (國明亭侯).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Later, as he made more contributions in battles, he was further promoted to _____-General (都護將軍)
Cao Hong.fact: Later, as he made more contributions in battles, he was further promoted to Protector-General (都護將軍).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Wu Lan was slain by _____ (強端), a Di chieftain from Yinping (陰平)
Cao Hong.fact: Wu Lan was slain by Qiangduan (強端), a Di chieftain from Yinping (陰平).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: Later that year, his son and successor _____ ended the Eastern Han dynasty and established the state of Cao Wei with himself as the emperor
Cao Hong.fact: Later that year, his son and successor Cao Pi ended the Eastern Han dynasty and set up the state of Cao Wei with himself as the emperor. Cao Pi appointed Cao Hong as General of the Guards (衞將軍) and promoted him to General of Agile Cavalry (驃騎將軍).

Cao Hong.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Hong.question: When Cao Cao was still the _____ of Works, he set an example by getting the county offices to keep records of the accounts of officials, including his
Cao Hong.fact: When Cao Cao was still the Minister of Works, he set an example by getting the county offices to keep records of the accounts of officials, including his. When his ministers tried to persuade him to spare Cao Hong, Cao Pi refused to listen.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: The _____ was Emperor of Cao Wei from 260 to 266.
Cao Huan.fact: Cao Huan () (246 – 302/303), courtesy name Jingming, was the fifth and last emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period. After his abdication, Cao Huan was granted the title "Prince of Chenliu" and held it until his death, after which he was posthumously honoured as "Emperor Yuan (of Cao Wei)".

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: On 4 _____ 266, he abdicated the throne in favour of regent Sima Yan (later Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty), and brought an end to the Wei regime
Cao Huan.fact: On 4 February 266, he abdicated the throne in favour of regent Sima Yan (later Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty), and brought an end to the Wei regime.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: His father, _____, the Prince of Yan, was a son of Cao Cao, the father of Wei's first emperor, Cao Pi
Cao Huan.fact: His father, Cao Yu, the Prince of Yan, was a son of Cao Cao, the father of Wei's first emperor, Cao Pi.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In late 263, _____, then Shu emperor, surrendered to Deng, bringing an end to the state of Shu
Cao Huan.fact: In late 263, Liu Shan, then Shu emperor, surrendered to Deng, bringing an end to the state of Shu.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: After the fall of Shu, _____ was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command
Cao Huan.fact: While Jiang Wei's attacks were largely easily repelled, Sima Zhao eventually ordered a counterattack on Shu with an invading force of 180,000 men commanded by Zhong Hui and Deng Ai. After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In early 264, _____ plotted with Jiang Wei to restore Shu and eliminate all the Wei generals who might oppose him
Cao Huan.fact: While Jiang Wei's attacks were largely easily repelled, Sima Zhao eventually ordered a counterattack on Shu with an invading force of 180,000 men commanded by Zhong Hui and Deng Ai. After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: However, the generals started a counterinsurgency and killed _____ and Jiang Wei
Cao Huan.fact: After the fall of Shu, Deng Ai was framed for treason by Zhong Hui and stripped of command. In early 264, Zhong Hui plotted with Jiang Wei to restore Shu and eliminate all the Wei generals who might oppose him.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Shu's former territories (in present-day _____, Chongqing, Yunnan, southern Shaanxi, and southeastern Gansu) were completely annexed by Wei
Cao Huan.fact: Shu's former territories (in present-day Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, southern Shaanxi, and southeastern Gansu) were completely annexed by Wei.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: In May 264, _____ became a vassal king under the title "King of Jin" — the final step before usurpation
Cao Huan.fact: In December 263, Sima Zhao again forced Cao Huan to grant him the nine bestowments and this time he finally accepted, signifying that a usurpation was near; at the same time he was also made Duke of Jin. In May 264, Sima Zhao became a vassal king under the title "King of Jin" — the final step before usurpation.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Sima Yan then established the Jin dynasty on 8 _____
Cao Huan.fact: After Sima Zhao died in September 265, his son, Sima Yan, inherited his father's position and on 4 February 266 forced Cao Huan to abdicate. Sima Yan then set up the Jin dynasty on 8 February.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: Sima Yan (posthumously known as _____ of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies
Cao Huan.fact: Sima Yan (posthumously called Emperor Wu of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies. He died in 302 during the reign of Emperor Wu's son, Emperor Hui.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He died in 302 during the reign of _____'s son, Emperor Hui
Cao Huan.fact: Sima Yan (posthumously called Emperor Wu of Jin) permitted him to retain imperial banners and wagons and to worship ancestors with imperial ceremonies. He died in 302 during the reign of Emperor Wu's son, Emperor Hui.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He was buried with honours due an emperor and given the posthumous name "_____" by the Jin court
Cao Huan.fact: He was buried with honours due an emperor and given the posthumous name "Yuan" by the Jin court.

Cao Huan.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Huan.question: He was succeeded by his son, _____, whose title was confirmed on 24 November 363
Cao Huan.fact: He was succeeded by his son, Cao Hui, whose title was confirmed on 24 November 363.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: The _____ was Chinese general and warlord (1862–1938).
Cao Kun.fact: General Cao Kun (simplified Chinese: 曹锟; traditional Chinese: 曹錕; pinyin: Cáo Kūn; Wade–Giles: Ts'ao K'un; courtesy name: Zhongshan (仲珊); December 12, 1862 – May 15, 1938) was a Chinese warlord and politician, who served as the President of China from 1923 to 1924, as well as the military leader of the Zhili clique in the Beiyang Army.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: During the First Sino-Japanese War in _____, he went with the army to fight in Joseon
Cao Kun.fact: During the First Sino-Japanese War in 1894, he went with the army to fight in Joseon.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: After the war was over he joined _____ to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army)
Cao Kun.fact: After the war was over he joined Yuan Shikai to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army).

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Admired by _____, Cao managed to rise very quickly
Cao Kun.fact: After the war was over he joined Yuan Shikai to participate in the training of the New Army (known as the Beiyang Army). Admired by Yuan, Cao managed to rise very quickly.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: By the time of the _____ Xinhai Revolution he commanded the Beiyang 3rd Division
Cao Kun.fact: By the time of the 1911 Xinhai Revolution he commanded the Beiyang 3rd Division.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He was a staunch supporter of _____, an opponent of liberalism and communism
Cao Kun.fact: He was a staunch supporter of Confucianism, an opponent of liberalism and communism.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He was made a general in the _____ and led the Zhili clique after the death of Feng Guozhang
Cao Kun.fact: He was made a general in the Beiyang Army and led the Zhili clique after the death of Feng Guozhang.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: During the _____ election he was promised the vice-presidency by Duan Qirui but the office remained vacant after most of the National Assembly left, depriving it of a quorum
Cao Kun.fact: During the 1918 election he was promised the vice-presidency by Duan Qirui but the office remained vacant after most of the National Assembly left, depriving it of a quorum.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He felt betrayed by Duan and defeated him in battle in _____
Cao Kun.fact: He felt betrayed by Duan and defeated him in battle in 1920.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: After forcing the resignations of both Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong, and engaging in bribery, he became president of China (in Beijing) on 10 October _____, serving to 2 November 1924
Cao Kun.fact: After forcing the resignations of both Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong, and engaging in bribery, he became president of China (in Beijing) on 10 October 1923, serving to 2 November 1924.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Unfortunately, the airline's 3-day trial tour ended in disaster: the plane crashed on approach to _____, killing all 14 onboard
Cao Kun.fact: After forcing the resignations of both Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong, and engaging in bribery, he became president of China (in Beijing) on 10 October 1923, serving to 2 November 1924. Unfortunately, the airline's 3-day trial tour ended in disaster: the plane crashed on approach to Beijing, killing all 14 onboard.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Cao had a family connection to the _____ military commander Ma Fuxing, who resided in Xinjiang
Cao Kun.fact: Cao had a family connection to the Chinese Muslim military commander Ma Fuxing, who resided in Xinjiang.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: That episode brought disrepute to the Beiyang government and the _____, which lacked a quorum even to hold elections
Cao Kun.fact: That episode brought disrepute to the Beiyang government and the National Assembly, which lacked a quorum even to hold elections.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Relations with his chief protégé, _____, soured and there were rumors of an impending split within the Zhili clique, but they stayed together to fight against the Fengtian clique
Cao Kun.fact: Relations with his chief protégé, Wu Peifu, soured and there were rumors of an impending split within the Zhili clique, but they stayed together to fight against the Fengtian clique.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: He promulgated the draft _____ Constitution of China in an effort to legitimize his presidential claim
Cao Kun.fact: He promulgated the draft 1923 Constitution of China in an effort to legitimize his presidential claim.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: During the Second Zhili-Fengtian War against Zhang Zuolin in October _____, Cao was betrayed and imprisoned by one of his own officers, General Feng Yuxiang, in the Beijing coup
Cao Kun.fact: During the Second Zhili-Fengtian War against Zhang Zuolin in October 1924, Cao was betrayed and imprisoned by one of his own officers, General Feng Yuxiang, in the Beijing coup.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Feng occupied _____ and forced Cao to resign
Cao Kun.fact: During the Second Zhili-Fengtian War against Zhang Zuolin in October 1924, Cao was betrayed and imprisoned by one of his own officers, General Feng Yuxiang, in the Beijing coup. Feng occupied Beijing and forced Cao to resign.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: His brother, _____, committed suicide while he was under house arrest
Cao Kun.fact: His brother, Cao Rui, committed suicide while he was under house arrest.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: In _____, Cao Kun was released from captivity as a goodwill gesture by Feng to Wu Peifu
Cao Kun.fact: In 1926, Cao Kun was released from captivity as a goodwill gesture by Feng to Wu Peifu.

Cao Kun.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Kun.question: Cao died in his home at Tianjin in May _____
Cao Kun.fact: Cao died in his home at Tianjin in May 1938.

Cao Lu.fact: Cao Lu (Chinese: 曹璐; born August 30, 1987) is a Chinese singer, actress, and television personality.

Cao Lu.fact: Cao Lu (Chinese: 曹璐; born August 30, 1987) is a Chinese singer, actress, and television personality.

Cao Lu.fact: She was a member of the South Korean girl group Fiestar until her group's disbandment in 2018 and regrouped in August 22, 2024.

Cao Lu.question: She released her independent extended play "Cat(貓咪)" in _____
Cao Lu.fact: She released her independent extended play "Cat(貓咪)" in 2004.

Cao Lu.fact: In February 2016, Cao Lu was cast in MBC's Real Men for the female soldier edition. In the same month, she was confirmed to cast in We Got Married along with comedian Jo Se-ho as a couple, which she departed from in September 2016.

Cao Lu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Lu.question: In the same month, she was confirmed to cast in We Got Married along with comedian Jo Se-ho as a couple, which she departed from in September _____
Cao Lu.fact: In February 2016, Cao Lu was cast in MBC's Real Men for the female soldier edition. In the same month, she was confirmed to cast in We Got Married along with comedian Jo Se-ho as a couple, which she departed from in September 2016.

Cao Lu.fact: In 2017, Cao Lu collaborated with Yerin and Kisum on the single "Spring Again".

Cao Lu.fact: On May 15, 2018, Fave Entertainment announced that Fiestar would be disbanded due to the expiration of the other members' contracts on April 30, 2018.

Cao Lu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Lu.question: In March _____, EE-Media announced on Weibo that Cao Lu had joined its ranks
Cao Lu.fact: In March 2021, EE-Media announced on Weibo that Cao Lu had joined its ranks.

Cao Lu.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Lu.question: On August 22, _____, Fiestar announced to make comeback to celebrate their 12th anniversary debut and Lu will restart group activities with Fiestar after 6 years
Cao Lu.fact: On August 22, 2024, Fiestar announced to make comeback to celebrate their 12th anniversary debut and Lu will restart group activities with Fiestar after 6 years.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: The _____ was Cao Wei emperor from 254 to 260.
Cao Mao.fact: Cao Mao (; 241 – 2 June 260), courtesy name Yanshi, was the fourth emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China. Described as intelligent and studious, Cao Mao made repeated attempts to seize back state power from the regent Sima Zhao but failed.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: He was a grandson of _____, the first emperor of Wei
Cao Mao.fact: He was a grandson of Cao Pi, the first emperor of Wei.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: He was killed in an abortive coup d'état against _____
Cao Mao.fact: Described as intelligent and studious, Cao Mao made repeated attempts to seize back state power from the regent Sima Zhao but failed. He was killed in an abortive coup d'état against Sima Zhao.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: By 254, state power was in the control of the Sima clan, whose patriarch Sima Yi had seized power from the regent _____ in 249
Cao Mao.fact: By 254, state power was in the control of the Sima clan, whose patriarch Sima Yi had seized power from the regent Cao Shuang in 249.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: In 254, after falsely accusing _____'s father-in-law Zhang Ji and Zhang's associates Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan of treason, Sima Shi had them and their clans executed
Cao Mao.fact: In 254, after falsely accusing Cao Fang's father-in-law Zhang Ji and Zhang's associates Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan of treason, Sima Shi had them and their clans executed. When Cao Fang himself considered a coup against the Simas later that year, Sima Shi had him deposed.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: When Cao Fang himself considered a coup against the Simas later that year, _____ had him deposed
Cao Mao.fact: After Sima Yi's death in 251, the Sima clan was led by his eldest son, Sima Shi. In 254, after falsely accusing Cao Fang's father-in-law Zhang Ji and Zhang's associates Li Feng and Xiahou Xuan of treason, Sima Shi had them and their clans executed.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Wen Qin and his sons, _____ and Wen Hu (文虎), fled to the rival state of Eastern Wu
Cao Mao.fact: Wen Qin and his sons, Wen Yang and Wen Hu (文虎), fled to the rival state of Eastern Wu.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: He issued an imperial edict for _____'s successor, Sima Zhao, to remain at Xuchang using the excuse that the situation at Shouchun was still not completely peaceful
Cao Mao.fact: Sima Shi died of illness shortly after the rebellion was suppressed. In the aftermath of Sima Shi's death, a 14-year-old Cao Mao made another effort to seize back state power.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: He also recalled _____'s assistant, Fu Gu, to return to the capital with the troops
Cao Mao.fact: He issued an imperial edict for Sima Shi's successor, Sima Zhao, to remain at Xuchang using the excuse that the situation at Shouchun was still not completely peaceful. He also recalled Sima Zhao's assistant, Fu Gu, to return to the capital with the troops.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: However, on the advice of _____ and Zhong Hui, Sima Zhao ignored the edict and returned to Luoyang and continued to remain in control of the government
Cao Mao.fact: He also recalled Sima Zhao's assistant, Fu Gu, to return to the capital with the troops. However, on the advice of Fu Gu and Zhong Hui, Sima Zhao ignored the edict and returned to Luoyang and continued to remain in control of the government.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: In addition, he gave _____ a fast two-wheeled wagon and five imperial guardsmen as escorts because Sima Wang lived further away from the palace than the others
Cao Mao.fact: In addition, he gave Sima Wang a fast two-wheeled wagon and five imperial guardsmen as escorts because Sima Wang lived further away from the palace than the others.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Around 257, _____, who replaced Guanqiu Jian as military commander in Shouchun, started a rebellion against Sima Zhao with support from the rival state of Eastern Wu
Cao Mao.fact: Around 257, Zhuge Dan, who replaced Guanqiu Jian as military commander in Shouchun, started a rebellion against Sima Zhao with support from the rival state of Eastern Wu. Internal conflict broke out in Shouchun between Zhuge Dan and Wen Qin which concluded with Wen Qin's death at Zhuge Dan's hands and the defection of Wen Qin's sons to Sima Zhao.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Internal conflict broke out in Shouchun between _____ and Wen Qin which concluded with Wen Qin's death at Zhuge Dan's hands and the defection of Wen Qin's sons to Sima Zhao
Cao Mao.fact: Around 257, Zhuge Dan, who replaced Guanqiu Jian as military commander in Shouchun, started a rebellion against Sima Zhao with support from the rival state of Eastern Wu. Internal conflict broke out in Shouchun between Zhuge Dan and Wen Qin which concluded with Wen Qin's death at Zhuge Dan's hands and the defection of Wen Qin's sons to Sima Zhao.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Shouchun eventually fell to _____'s forces and the rebellion was effectively crushed
Cao Mao.fact: Around 257, Zhuge Dan, who replaced Guanqiu Jian as military commander in Shouchun, started a rebellion against Sima Zhao with support from the rival state of Eastern Wu. Sima Zhao led an army to suppress the revolt and trapped the rebels in the city by early 258.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Wang Shen and _____ went to warn Sima Zhao
Cao Mao.fact: Cao Mao gathered his associates Wang Shen, Wang Jing and Wang Ye, and announced his plan for a last effort against Sima Zhao to regain his power. Wang Shen and Wang Ye went to warn Sima Zhao.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Sima Zhao also retroactively declined his title as _____ of Jin and the nine bestowments
Cao Mao.fact: Sima Zhao with his uncle, Sima Fu, and the other high ministers then requested Sima Zhao to have Cao Mao posthumously reinstated as a duke and buried with honours befitting a prince – for appearances of leniency. Sima Zhao also retroactively declined his title as Duke of Jin and the nine bestowments.

Cao Mao.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Mao.question: Sima Zhao blamed _____ for the regicide, and ordered his familial extermination
Cao Mao.fact: Sima Zhao blamed Cheng Ji for the regicide, and ordered his familial extermination.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: The _____ was Emperor of Cao Wei of China (220 - 226).
Cao Pi.fact: Cao Pi () (c.late 187 – 29 June 226), courtesy name Zihuan, was the first emperor of the state of Cao Wei in the Three Kingdoms period of China.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: He was the second son of Cao Cao, a warlord who lived in the late _____ dynasty, but the eldest son among all the children born to Cao Cao by his concubine (later wife), Lady Bian
Cao Pi.fact: He was the second son of Cao Cao, a warlord who lived in the late Eastern Han dynasty, but the eldest son among all the children born to Cao Cao by his concubine (later wife), Lady Bian.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: After the defeat of Cao Cao's rival _____ at the Battle of Guandu, he took Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen, as a concubine, but in 221 Lady Zhen died and Guo Nüwang became empress
Cao Pi.fact: After the defeat of Cao Cao's rival Yuan Shao at the Battle of Guandu, he took Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen, as a concubine, but in 221 Lady Zhen died and Guo Nüwang became empress.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: During his reign, he formally established _____'s nine-rank system as the base for civil service nomination, which drew many talents into his government
Cao Pi.fact: During his reign, he formally set up Chen Qun's nine-rank system as the base for civil service nomination, which drew many talents into his government.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: He wrote _____ (燕歌行), the first Chinese poem in the style of seven syllables per line (七言詩)
Cao Pi.fact: He wrote Yan Ge Xing (燕歌行), the first Chinese poem in the style of seven syllables per line (七言詩).

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: After Cao Cao defeated _____ then conquered the city of Ye and massacred his population
Cao Pi.fact: After Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shang then conquered the city of Ye and massacred his population.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: This position placed him second to his father, who was then _____ (丞相) and the de facto head of government in China
Cao Pi.fact: This position placed him second to his father, who was then Imperial Chancellor (丞相) and the de facto head of government in China.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: Cao Cao greatly favoured _____ (his third son with Lady Bian), who was known for his literary talents
Cao Pi.fact: Cao Cao greatly favoured Cao Zhi (his third son with Lady Bian), who was known for his literary talents. Both Cao Pi and Cao Zhi were talented poets, but Cao Zhi was more highly regarded as a poet and speaker.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: Cui Yan was executed, while _____ was deposed
Cao Pi.fact: Initially, Cao Zhi's party appeared to be prevailing, and in 216 they were successful in falsely accusing two officials supporting Cao Pi—Cui Yan and Mao Jie. Cui Yan was executed, while Mao Jie was deposed.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: The apprehension was particularly heightened when, after Cao Cao's death, the _____ under the general Zang Ba suddenly deserted, leaving Luoyang and returning home
Cao Pi.fact: The apprehension was particularly heightened when, after Cao Cao's death, the Qingzhou Corps under the general Zang Ba suddenly deserted, leaving Luoyang and returning home.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: With the help of _____, the political situation soon stabilised
Cao Pi.fact: With the help of Jiang Ji, the political situation soon stabilised.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: This event marked the official end of the Han dynasty and the beginning of the _____ period
Cao Pi.fact: This event marked the official end of the Han dynasty and the beginning of the Three Kingdoms period.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: The dethroned _____ was granted the title "Duke of Shanyang" (山陽公)
Cao Pi.fact: Emperor Xian did so, and Cao Pi formally declined three times (a model that would be followed by future usurpers in Chinese history), and then finally accepted on 25 November of that year, establishing the state of Cao Wei. The dethroned Emperor Xian was granted the title "Duke of Shanyang" (山陽公).

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: He also moved the imperial capital from _____ to Luoyang
Cao Pi.fact: He also moved the imperial capital from Xuchang to Luoyang.

Cao Pi.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Pi.question: Sun Quan, who controlled the vast majority of southeastern and southern _____, did not take any affirmative steps one way or another, leaving his options open
Cao Pi.fact: Sun Quan, who controlled the vast majority of southeastern and southern China, did not take any affirmative steps one way or another, leaving his options open.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: The _____ was Chinese Han dynasty and Cao Wei general (168–223).
Cao Ren.fact: Cao Ren () (168 – 6 May 223), courtesy name Zixiao, was a military general serving during the late Eastern Han dynasty of China under the warlord Cao Cao, who was also his older second cousin.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: He continued serving in the state of _____ – founded by Cao Cao's son and successor, Cao Pi – during the Three Kingdoms period
Cao Ren.fact: He continued serving in the state of Cao Wei – set up by Cao Cao's son and successor, Cao Pi – during the Three Kingdoms period.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: He was appointed as the _____ (大司馬) when Cao Pi ascended the throne, and was also credited by the latter for the establishment of Wei
Cao Ren.fact: He was appointed as the Grand Marshal (大司馬) when Cao Pi ascended the throne, and was also credited by the latter for the establishment of Wei.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: His grandfather _____ (曹襃) and father Cao Chi (曹熾) served in the government of the Eastern Han dynasty
Cao Ren.fact: His grandfather Cao Bao (曹襃) and father Cao Chi (曹熾) served in the government of the Eastern Han dynasty.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: He had a younger full brother, _____
Cao Ren.fact: He had a younger full brother, Cao Chun. As their father died when they were still young, Cao Ren and Cao Chun lived with another family.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: He made great contributions in the campaign against _____ between 197 and 199
Cao Ren.fact: He made great contributions in the campaign against Yuan Shu between 197 and 199.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: After Cao Cao had defeated the _____ rebels, he received Emperor Xian (who had escaped from the clutches of Li Jue and Guo Si) and set up the new capital at Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan) in 196
Cao Ren.fact: After Cao Cao had defeated the Yellow Turban rebels, he received Emperor Xian (who had escaped from the clutches of Li Jue and Guo Si) and set up the new capital at Xu (許; present-day Xuchang, Henan) in 196.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao Cao initially, but rebelled later and launched a surprise attack, which led to the Battle of _____
Cao Ren.fact: The following year, Cao Ren followed Cao Cao on a campaign against the warlord Zhang Xiu, and was authorised to lead a separate force to raid the counties around Zhang Xiu's base in Wan (宛; or Wancheng, present-day Wancheng District, Nanyang, Henan) and he captured over 3,000 civilians. Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao Cao initially, but rebelled later and launched a surprise attack, which led to the Battle of Wancheng.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Cao Cao was defeated and he retreated after his forces succeeded in repelling further attacks by _____
Cao Ren.fact: The following year, Cao Ren followed Cao Cao on a campaign against the warlord Zhang Xiu, and was authorised to lead a separate force to raid the counties around Zhang Xiu's base in Wan (宛; or Wancheng, present-day Wancheng District, Nanyang, Henan) and he captured over 3,000 civilians. Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao Cao initially, but rebelled later and launched a surprise attack, which led to the Battle of Wancheng.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: However, as they were withdrawing, _____ attacked again and Cao Cao's men were unable to drive the enemy away
Cao Ren.fact: The following year, Cao Ren followed Cao Cao on a campaign against the warlord Zhang Xiu, and was authorised to lead a separate force to raid the counties around Zhang Xiu's base in Wan (宛; or Wancheng, present-day Wancheng District, Nanyang, Henan) and he captured over 3,000 civilians. Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao Cao initially, but rebelled later and launched a surprise attack, which led to the Battle of Wancheng.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: Yuan Shao attempted to cut off Cao Cao's route to the west by sending _____ (韓猛) southwest
Cao Ren.fact: Yuan Shao attempted to cut off Cao Cao's route to the west by sending Han Meng (韓猛) southwest. Cao Ren responded to the threat by defeating Han Meng at Jiluo Hill (雞洛山; located 50 li northeast of present-day Xinmi, Henan).

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: During one battle near _____ (壺關; present-day Huguan County, Shanxi), Cao Cao gave orders that all the enemy troops would be buried alive after the city fell
Cao Ren.fact: During one battle near Hu Pass (壺關; present-day Huguan County, Shanxi), Cao Cao gave orders that all the enemy troops would be buried alive after the city fell.

Cao Ren.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Ren.question: However, unlike what everyone thought, _____ managed to create havoc around the Wu's army with just 100 men left by then
Cao Ren.fact: Cao Ren was aware that his army's morale was low, since they were recently defeated at Red Cliffs, so he ordered his subordinate Niu Jin to lead 300 volunteer soldiers into battle, in the hope that they would display bravery and boost his men's morale. Niu Jin and his men were heavily outnumbered and surrounded by the enemy.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: The _____ was Emperor of Cao Wei from 226 to 239.
Cao Rui.fact: Cao Rui () (204 or 205 – 22 January 239), courtesy name Yuanzhong, was the second emperor of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period. Based on conflicting accounts of his age, Pei Songzhi calculated that, in order to be Cao Pi's son, Cao Rui could not have been 36 (by East Asian age reckoning) when he died as recorded, so the recorded age was in error; late-Qing scholars Lu Bi (卢弼) and Mao Guangsheng (冒广生) argued instead that Cao Rui was Yuan Xi's son.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: His parentage is in dispute: his mother, _____, was Yuan Xi's wife, but she later remarried Cao Pi, the first ruler of Wei
Cao Rui.fact: His parentage is in dispute: his mother, Lady Zhen, was Yuan Xi's wife, but she later remarried Cao Pi, the first ruler of Wei.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He devoted many resources into building palaces and ancestral temples, and his reign saw the stalemate between his empire, _____, and Eastern Wu become more entrenched
Cao Rui.fact: He devoted many resources into building palaces and ancestral temples, and his reign saw the stalemate between his empire, Shu Han, and Eastern Wu become more entrenched.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He passed the throne to his adopted son _____ and entrusted him to the regency of Cao Shuang and Sima Yi
Cao Rui.fact: He passed the throne to his adopted son Cao Fang and entrusted him to the regency of Cao Shuang and Sima Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Sima Yi became in control of the Wei government from _____ 249, eventually allowing his grandson Sima Yan to usurp the throne in February 266
Cao Rui.fact: Sima Yi became in control of the Wei government from February 249, eventually allowing his grandson Sima Yan to usurp the throne in February 266.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: His father _____ was Cao Cao's oldest surviving son and the heir apparent
Cao Rui.fact: His father Cao Pi was Cao Cao's oldest surviving son and the heir apparent. His mother Lady Zhen had been the wife of Yuan Shao's son Yuan Xi, but when she was seized by Cao Cao's army in c.mid-September 204, Cao Pi forced her to marry him, and she gave birth to Cao Rui only eight months after the wedding—leading to theories that Cao Rui was actually biologically Yuan Xi's son and not Cao Pi's.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Lady Zhen was not allowed to accompany him to the new capital _____; in August 221, he forced her to commit suicide
Cao Rui.fact: Lady Zhen was not allowed to accompany him to the new capital Luoyang; in August 221, he forced her to commit suicide.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Sometime during his years as the Prince of _____, he married a daughter of an aristocrat, Lady Yu, as his wife and princess
Cao Rui.fact: Because of what happened to Lady Zhen and Cao Rui's unclear origin, even though Cao Rui was the oldest of Cao Pi's sons, he was not created crown prince early in his father's reign, but was only created the Prince of Pingyuan in March 222. Sometime during his years as the Prince of Pingyuan, he married a daughter of an aristocrat, Lady Yu, as his wife and princess.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He apparently had a cordial relationship with _____, who was created empress (in October 222); as she was sonless, his status as heir apparent was not seriously challenged
Cao Rui.fact: He apparently had a cordial relationship with Lady Guo, who was created empress (in October 222); as she was sonless, his status as heir apparent was not seriously challenged.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: His father had appointed three regents for him—his distant cousin _____, the steady administrator Chen Qun, and the shrewd strategist Sima Yi
Cao Rui.fact: His father had appointed three regents for him—his distant cousin Cao Zhen, the steady administrator Chen Qun, and the shrewd strategist Sima Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: Ultimately, Zhuge's campaigns were futile; after his death in 234, his plan was largely abandoned by his successors _____ and Fei Yi
Cao Rui.fact: Ultimately, Zhuge's campaigns were futile; after his death in 234, his plan was largely abandoned by his successors Jiang Wan and Fei Yi.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: However, that did not mean that there was peace on the borders with _____, as nearly every year, there would be battles between the two states
Cao Rui.fact: However, that did not mean that there was peace on the borders with Shu Han, as nearly every year, there would be battles between the two states.

Cao Rui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Rui.question: He also entrusted the southeastern border to the capable _____, and Man's stewardship averted many disasters
Cao Rui.fact: He also entrusted the southeastern border to the capable Man Chong, and Man's stewardship averted many disasters.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: The _____ was Chinese politician (died 190 BCE).
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Shen or Cao Can (died 24 September 190 BCE), courtesy name Jingbo (Chinese: 敬伯), was a Chinese military general and politician.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: He served as a chancellor of the _____ dynasty
Cao Shen.fact: He served as a chancellor of the Western Han dynasty.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: He participated in the Chu–_____ on Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu of Han)'s side and contributed greatly to the founding of the Han dynasty
Cao Shen.fact: He participated in the Chu–Han Contention on Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu of Han)'s side and contributed greatly to the founding of the Han dynasty.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Once, _____ was tasked with escorting some convicts to Mount Li to become labourers, but some prisoners escaped and Liu was forced to become a fugitive
Cao Shen.fact: He participated in the Chu–Han Contention on Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu of Han)'s side and contributed greatly to the founding of the Han dynasty. He was a close friend of Liu Bang.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: However, the magistrate changed his mind later and denied _____ entry into the city
Cao Shen.fact: Once, Liu Bang was tasked with escorting some convicts to Mount Li to become labourers, but some prisoners escaped and Liu was forced to become a fugitive. In 209 BC, after the Dazexiang Uprising broke out, the magistrate of Pei County considered rebelling against the Qin dynasty as well, so he heeded Cao Shen and Xiao He's advice to invite Liu Bang back to support him.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: The townsfolk rebelled against the magistrate and killed him, allowing _____ and his men to enter
Cao Shen.fact: In 209 BC, after the Dazexiang Uprising broke out, the magistrate of Pei County considered rebelling against the Qin dynasty as well, so he heeded Cao Shen and Xiao He's advice to invite Liu Bang back to support him. However, the magistrate changed his mind later and denied Liu Bang entry into the city.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: He returned to help _____, who was trapped at Yongqiu, and defeated Li You, the Qin general defending Sanchuan
Cao Shen.fact: The townsfolk rebelled against the magistrate and killed him, allowing Liu Bang and his men to enter. Liu Bang built up his rebel army in Pei County and Cao Shen served as one of his advisors.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: They scored victories against _____'s forces, the Zhao army at the Battle of Jingxing, and the combined forces of Qi and Chu at the Battle of Wei River
Cao Shen.fact: They scored victories against Wei Bao's forces, the Zhao army at the Battle of Jingxing, and the combined forces of Qi and Chu at the Battle of Wei River.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: In 202 BC, _____ defeated Xiang Yu at the Battle of Gaixia and unified China under his rule
Cao Shen.fact: During this time, Cao Shen was appointed as acting-Left Chancellor of Liu Bang's Han kingdom, and subsequently promoted to Right Chancellor. After the conquest of the Qi kingdom, Cao Shen left Han Xin and returned to Liu Bang's side to join him in resisting Xiang Yu.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Liu Bang became the _____ and his dynasty was named "Han"
Cao Shen.fact: Liu Bang became the Emperor and his dynasty was named "Han". He was historically called "Emperor Gao" (or Emperor Gaozu).

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: He was historically known as "_____" (or Emperor Gaozu)
Cao Shen.fact: He was historically called "Emperor Gao" (or Emperor Gaozu).

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: He was also conferred the title of "_____ of Pingyang" (平陽侯) and given 10,630 households in his marquisate
Cao Shen.fact: He was also conferred the title of "Marquis of Pingyang" (平陽侯) and given 10,630 households in his marquisate.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: In 196 BC, he commanded the Qi forces that assisted the emperor in suppressing _____'s rebellion in Dai (present-day northern Shanxi and northwestern Hebei)
Cao Shen.fact: In 196 BC, he commanded the Qi forces that assisted the emperor in suppressing Chen Xi's rebellion in Dai (present-day northern Shanxi and northwestern Hebei).

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: This became the origin of a Chinese idiom, _____ (萧规曹随; lit
Cao Shen.fact: This became the origin of a Chinese idiom, Xiao Gui Cao Sui (萧规曹随; lit.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: "Cao following _____'s rules"), which is used to describe the continuation of the work of one's predecessor
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Shen spent his time drinking and feasting, and maintained well Xiao He's system of governance but did not implement any new changes. When Emperor Hui asked him why he did not change the system, Cao Shen replied that he was not as good as Xiao He and did not want to make changes for fear of negatively affecting the system left behind by Xiao.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Cao Zhu was in turn succeeded by his son, _____ (曹奇; died 153 BC), who helped Emperor Jing suppress the Rebellion of the Seven States
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Zhu was in turn succeeded by his son, Cao Qi (曹奇; died 153 BC), who helped Emperor Jing suppress the Rebellion of the Seven States. Cao Qi's son, Cao Shi (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters.

Cao Shen.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shen.question: Cao Qi's son, _____ (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters
Cao Shen.fact: Cao Qi's son, Cao Shi (曹時; died 131 BC), married Princess Pingyang, one of Emperor Jing's daughters. Cao Shi's son, Cao Xiang (曹襄; died 115 BC), married Princess Wei (a daughter of Emperor Wu and Empress Wei Zifu) and served as a general in the Han campaigns against the Xiongnu.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: The _____ was Chinese general and Cao Wei regent (died 249).
Cao Shuang.fact: Cao Shuang (died 9 February 249), courtesy name Zhaobo, was a Chinese military general and regent of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He was the eldest son of _____, a prominent general of Cao Wei
Cao Shuang.fact: He was the eldest son of Cao Zhen, a prominent general of Cao Wei.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He initially held great power in _____ as General-in-Chief but later lost his power to Sima Yi in the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs and was executed on charges of treason
Cao Shuang.fact: Cao Shuang (died 9 February 249), courtesy name Zhaobo, was a Chinese military general and regent of the state of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period of China. He was the eldest son of Cao Zhen, a prominent general of Cao Wei.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: After ascending the throne in June 226, _____ bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign
Cao Shuang.fact: When Cao Rui was still his father's heir, he favored Cao Shuang greatly. After ascending the throne in June 226, Cao Rui bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: Around 239, when the Wei emperor _____ became critically ill, he resolved to pass the throne to his adopted son, Cao Fang
Cao Shuang.fact: When Cao Rui was still his father's heir, he favored Cao Shuang greatly. After ascending the throne in June 226, Cao Rui bestowed upon Shuang several titles of increasing seniority and prestige over his reign.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: However, his trusted officials Liu Fang (劉放) and Sun Zi (孫資), who were unfriendly with Xiahou Xian and _____, became apprehensive upon hearing that Cao Rui wanted to appoint them as regents
Cao Shuang.fact: He initially wanted to entrust Cao Fang to his uncle Cao Yu, to serve as the lead regent, along with Xiahou Xian (夏侯獻), Cao Shuang, Cao Zhao (曹肇; son of Cao Xiu) and Qin Lang. However, his trusted officials Liu Fang (劉放) and Sun Zi (孫資), who were unfriendly with Xiahou Xian and Cao Zhao, became apprehensive upon hearing that Cao Rui wanted to appoint them as regents.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: He was also often at odds with his co-regent _____, who had greater influence and support
Cao Shuang.fact: He was also often at odds with his co-regent Sima Yi, who had greater influence and support. In 243, Sima Yi's position was further strengthened by another successful deployment: Zhuge Ke, a general of Wei's rival state, Eastern Wu, was constantly sending agents to Shouchun (壽春; around present-day Shou County, Anhui) to prepare an invasion, so Sima Yi led Wei forces to Shu County (舒縣), Lujiang Commandery (盧江郡) near the Wei–Wu border.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: Upon hearing the news, the Wu emperor _____ immediately ordered Zhuge Ke to withdraw to Chaisang (柴桑), Yuzhang Commandery (豫章郡)
Cao Shuang.fact: Upon hearing the news, the Wu emperor Sun Quan immediately ordered Zhuge Ke to withdraw to Chaisang (柴桑), Yuzhang Commandery (豫章郡).

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: While it was ostensibly a promotion for _____, the position of Grand Tutor was in fact an honorary one without any real authority over military affairs
Cao Shuang.fact: Sima Yi's popularity and influence instantly multiplied as he was cheered as being able to scare away the enemy numbering over 100,000 without a fight and thus secured the border and saved Shouchun from certain attack. Cao Shuang, feeling insecure over Sima Yi's triumph, managed to persuade the emperor Cao Fang to promote Sima Yi to the position of Grand Tutor (太傅).

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: However, two months later, he lost to Shu forces led by _____ and Fei Yi at the Battle of Xingshi and barely escaped back to Chang'an
Cao Shuang.fact: However, two months later, he lost to Shu forces led by Wang Ping and Fei Yi at the Battle of Xingshi and barely escaped back to Chang'an.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: At the same time, _____'s popularity and influence further increased due to his opposition to the campaign from the start
Cao Shuang.fact: At the same time, Sima Yi's popularity and influence further increased due to his opposition to the campaign from the start. Potentially to deceive Cao Shuang into letting down his guard, Sima Yi stopped engaging in any political activity in May 247 and retired on the grounds of illness.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: According to _____, Sima Yi misheard "Jing Province" as "Bing Province"
Cao Shuang.fact: In the winter of 248, Cao Shuang's protégé, Li Sheng, was appointed as the Inspector of Jing Province by the Wei imperial court. Cao Shuang and his followers overjoyed when Li Sheng reported that Sima Yi was indeed ill and that he could not even hear what Li Sheng said.

Cao Shuang.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shuang.question: After that, they proceeded to go on a hunting expedition outside _____
Cao Shuang.fact: On 5 February 249, Cao Shuang and his two brothers, Cao Xi (曹羲) and Cao Xun (曹訓), left the imperial capital Luoyang to accompany the emperor Cao Fang to pay respects to his ancestors at the Gaoping Tombs (高平陵). After that, they proceeded to go on a hunting expedition outside Luoyang.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: The _____ was Chinese poet, writer and translator.
Cao Shui.fact: Cao Shui (simplified Chinese: 曹谁; traditional Chinese: 曹誰; pinyin: Cáo Shuí; born June 5, 1982), also called Shawn Cao, courtesy name Yaou (Eurasian), pseudonym or hao Lord of Tower of Babel, is a Chinese poet, novelist, screenwriter and translator.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: He is one of the representative figures of _____
Cao Shui.fact: He is one of the representative figures of Chinese Contemporary Literature.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: In his Declaration of _____, he aims to integrate sacred and secular cultures, oriental and occidental cultures, ancient and modern cultures in Chinese literature
Cao Shui.fact: He leads the Great Poetry Movement. In his Declaration of Great Poetry, he aims to integrate sacred and secular cultures, oriental and occidental cultures, ancient and modern cultures in Chinese literature.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: His most notable works include the Epic of _____, Secret of Heaven (trilogy), and King Peacock (TV series)
Cao Shui.fact: His most notable works include the Epic of Eurasia, Secret of Heaven (trilogy), and King Peacock (TV series). His works are dedicated to rebuilding a republic in which the whole humanity can live in freedom, which he always described as Eurasia, the Top of the Tower of Babel or Kunlun Mountains (Heaven Mountains).

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: As of _____, 46 books of Cao Shui have been published, including 10 poem collections, 4 essay collections, 10 novels, 18 fairy tales, 4 translations and one hundred episodes TV series and films
Cao Shui.fact: As of 2024, 46 books of Cao Shui have been published, including 10 poem collections, 4 essay collections, 10 novels, 18 fairy tales, 4 translations and one hundred episodes TV series and films. His works have been translated into 26 languages by 2024.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: His works have been translated into 26 languages by _____
Cao Shui.fact: As of 2024, 46 books of Cao Shui have been published, including 10 poem collections, 4 essay collections, 10 novels, 18 fairy tales, 4 translations and one hundred episodes TV series and films. His works have been translated into 26 languages by 2024.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: He is a member of _____' Association, China Film Association, and World Poetry Movement
Cao Shui.fact: He is a member of China Writers' Association, China Film Association, and World Poetry Movement.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: He is also the editor-in-chief of _____ and deputy editor-in-chief of World Poetry
Cao Shui.fact: He is also the editor-in-chief of Great Poem and deputy editor-in-chief of World Poetry.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: Currently he lives in _____ as a professional writer and screenwriter
Cao Shui.fact: Currently he lives in Beijing as a professional writer and screenwriter.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: After his resignation, Shui traveled around Tibet and _____, places which he considers the center of both Eurasia or World
Cao Shui.fact: After his resignation, Shui traveled around Tibet and Xinjiang, places which he considers the center of both Eurasia or World.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: After returning to _____, he began his professional writing career
Cao Shui.fact: He received his bachelor's degree in Chinese literature at Qinghai University for Nationalities in 2006 and was an international editor of Xihai Metropolis Daily in Xining for two years until he resigned to pursue his desire for personal freedom. After returning to Xining, he began his professional writing career.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: In _____, he moved to Beijing
Cao Shui.fact: In 2017, he moved to Beijing.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: Until these days in _____, he has written 10 poem collections, 4 essay collections, 10 novels, 18 fairy tales, 4 translations, 100 episodes for TV, as well as scripts for plays and films
Cao Shui.fact: Until these days in 2024, he has written 10 poem collections, 4 essay collections, 10 novels, 18 fairy tales, 4 translations, 100 episodes for TV, as well as scripts for plays and films.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: He obtained his master's degree in literature from _____
Cao Shui.fact: He obtained his master's degree in literature from Beijing Normal University.

Cao Shui.subject: Indian Languages
Cao Shui.question: He is a member of the _____' Association, China Film Association, and China Poetry Society

Contra Celsum.fact: Origen replies to this by arguing that, since humans have become flesh, the Logos could not effectively reveal God to them without first becoming flesh itself. He states that this does not mean that the Logos originated from a human woman, but rather that it joined a human soul and body.

Contra Celsum.subject: Indian Languages
Contra Celsum.question: Instead, the similarities between _____ and Plato are merely the result of the fact that the Logos, incarnate in Jesus, sometimes inspired Plato
Contra Celsum.fact: Origen responds to Celsus's accusation that Jesus had performed his miracles using magic rather than divine powers by asserting that, unlike magicians, Jesus had not performed his miracles for show, but rather to reform his audiences. Origen defends Jesus's moral teachings against Celsus's accusation that they were merely plagiarized from Plato, stating that it is ridiculous to think that Jesus, a Galilean Jew, would have done such a thing.

Contra Celsum.subject: Indian Languages

Contra Celsum.subject: Indian Languages

Contra Celsum.fact: Most scholars reject Andresen's view that Origen falsified or intentionally misrepresented Celsus's work, noting that Origen's highly complex and philosophical refutations imply that he viewed Celsus as having a high level of intellectual competence and that he was worthy of a serious, scholarly response.
